title: AI for Public Good Lot 1 (Health: Innovative AI-based cancer imaging solutions for breast and prostate diagnosis) and Lot 2 (Energy: Innovative AI-based solutions for electric grid optimization)
description:
The European Commission is committed to tapping into the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to collaboratively and complementarily drive research to address global challenges. 
DG CONNECT is the European Commission’s Directorate General responsible for digital policies. Through its Directorate A “Artificial Intelligence Office”, it is tasked to implement the AI Act and promote the development and use of trustworthy AI. Additionally, it focuses on creating solutions for societal good, while also facilitating the implementation of international AI agreements to contribute to a global approach to AI. 
The purpose of this call for tenders is to develop and test AI-powered solutions for the benefit of the EU as well as wider communities and third countries. The call has two lots, on AI for Cancer imaging (LOT1) and on AI for Electric grid optimisation (LOT2).
LOT 1 will explore and demonstrate how AI-powered solutions applied to EU cancer imaging data can be further fine-tuned and applied in other locations and settings covering a large variety of populations, without transferring the underlying sensitive health data. It has two predefined use-cases, breast cancer and prostate cancer.
LOT2 will support the European Commission in exploring and demonstrating the application of AI- powered solutions to effectively tackle challenges within energy systems, specifically focusing on the seamless integration of renewable energy sources (RES) capacity across diverse energy system levels.

title: 81306308-Soutien à une gestion circulaire de l'eau urbaine au Maroc
description: The project "Circular economy in urban water management" is working in Morocco with the MATNUHPV (Ministry of Town and Country Planning, Housing and Urban Policy) at national level and in the cities of Marrakech and Tangier to integrate circular water management and climate-resilient water management into urban planning and development. This call for tender is intended to support the project in the following areas: - Analysis of urban vulnerability/resilience and modelling of scenarios Firstly, the service provider is tasked to analyse the vulnerability and resilience of the two cities (Marrakech and Tangier) in relation to climate change. This will make it possible to: i) qualitatively assess the vulnerability of the two cities to the risks associated with climate change by studying their exposure, sensitivity, and capacity to adapt, and ii) rank the level of vulnerability associated with the various impacts, in relation to the scale of the consequences and the probability of occurrence of these impacts. Subsequently, the service provider shall model two scenarios, one (1) for the city of Marrakech and one (1) for the city of Tangier, taking into account the "Referentiel" (national guidelines about circular water management) and the "cross diagnosis of urban water management". These two national services will be contracted in Morocco beforehand. - Application of the "Referentiel" about circular water management in two urban planning documents, one in Marrakech, one in Tangier. The aim of this phase is to integrate the principles of the circular water economy and ensure that the Framework is applied in an urban planning document currently being drawn up for the two cities, in order to promote sustainable management of water resources and ensure urban resilience in the face of water-related challenges. The aim is to ensure that the Framework for integrating the circular water economy is anchored in the local realities of the two Moroccan cities, promoting successful and sustainable implementation and drawing lessons on potential bottlenecks and shortcomings in its application - Development of an urban vision for circular water management, which is adopted by the city councils and based on the developed guidelines about circular water management as well as national and local rules and regulations. The objective of this part is to work in a participatory, inclusive and gender-sensitive process with the two cities of Marrakech and Tangier on the development of an urban/communal Vision for a future circular water economy in the two cities which is than translated into a concrete action plan. - Development of two "bankable" projects, one for each of the two cities, in the field of the circular economy of urban water, ready to be submitted to financial intermediaries. The selected projects derive from the city action plan (see above). Project preparation to "bankability" must be in line with IFIs (international financing institutions) financing requirements. - Integration of climate-sensitive and water-relevant data into the Ministry's Geoportal (GIS).The aim of this work package is to provide technical support to the Department of Urban Planning and to integrate the climate and water relevant GIS data of the two cities (Tangiers and Marrakesh) into the Ministry's Géoportail. Furthermore the technical basis (architecture, structures and data components) for the integration of an additional layer (climate and water relevant data) in the existing GIS system of the ministry are to be developed. - Capacity-development for relevant actors in the field of urban circular water management. The aim of this work package is to build the institutional and technical capacities of national partners, urban development agencies, local authorities, local water service providers and civil society to develop and integrate a circular water economy that is resilient to climate change into urban planning and development. It is intended to have two fulltime consultants, one for each city, and several expert-pools for water, digitalization/IT, project preparation and capacity development. One of the full-time experts will be the contractor's team leader. The service is planned to last for 18 months. Extension possible under certain circumstances.

title: RISC-V INSTRUCTION SET ARCHITECTURE SIMULATION MODEL AND EMULATION IN VIRTUAL PLATFORM FOR HARDWARE-SOFTWARE CODESIGN - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to develop a simulation model of a RISC-V (reduced instruction set computer) instruction set architecture (ISA) processor and peripherals, in a suitable hardware-software co-design environment, and perform design space exploration of a system-on-chip.Description:RISC-V is an open-source and royalty-free hardware instruction set architecture based on RISC principles. An open ISA is remarkably interesting for space due to several reasons: It reduces potential difficulties in license negotiation or export restrictions. It allows to perform modifications for radiation mitigation. It adds or modifies instructions to execute functions that are frequently required by space applications, such as bit manipulation, sub-word arithmetic, vector or SIMD (single instruction, multiple data) computations.RISC-V has been gaining popularity in the past years, and its use in space is now close to a reality thanks to several on-going system-on-chip (SoC) developments that will embed RISC-V multi core processor, along with several other interfaces to enable their use in satellite payloads and platforms, such as SpaceFibre, TM/TC (telemetry/telecommand) or cryptographic functions. The successful adoption of this architecture and embarking of the future SoC depends in a great extent on the features of the hardware, and on the availability of software development tool chains that enable the programming of the cores with suitable on-board software.Hardware and software developments around RISC-V can benefit greatly from the hardware-software co-design development flow, which simultaneously considers hardware and software within the design process. This enables the co-development and co-verification of hardware and software using simulation and/or emulation with the help of tools such as virtual platforms where simulation models of the processor ISA, and models of other components of the SoC can be executed at different levelsof abstraction, and with the required simulation speed. A fast ISA simulator of RISC-V facilitates early software development and the development software tool chains. All this before the first hardware prototypes are available.ESA has promoted the development of the SoCRocket virtual platform, which has been made available to missions and projects. This platform is comprised by several functional blocks, and can be used to simulate a SoC, but now, only LEON based systems are currently supported.This activity aims at developing a simulation model of RISC-V that can be executed in a suitable virtual platform at an appropriate abstraction level, easing the development of software, and enabling hardware-software co-design and design space exploration of a system-on-chip.The main tasks to be accomplished are: Assess the suitability of a virtual platform to simulate a RISC-V based SoC considering trade-offs related to accuracy of the models and simulation speed, SoCRocket and possible alternatives. Create a simulation model of the RISC-Vinstruction set, that can be integrated in a virtual platform, directly or through an emulator, and aid the development of software. Develop and integrate new functional blocks in a virtual platform, such as: SpaceFibre, TM/TC functions, cryptography, Ethernet. Design space exploration in a RISC-V based multicore model of a SoC.NOTE: This activity is currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The final list of participating states will be known at tender issue.
